ladder.what: 12 V input power of the whole card
ladder.gran: 10 mW; a new value every 133 ms
ladder.instrument: DM_CMD_GET_MODULE_POWER, or the SP stats trace
ladder.note: The host can poll much faster than the value changes (ettelem's six-command sample takes 22 ms), but the service processor refreshes once per loop pass. The PMIC (a closed ATSAMD20 firmware) does the averaging. The meter can be starved by the workload: rings between shires s and s+16 (nocbench xshire:16) slow the SP's management path from 22 ms to 150 ms per six-command telemetry sample and hold the board reading for seconds at a time on aifoundry2; the energy manual's analysis drops such bursts by the sampler's own latency.

ladder.what: Minion cores, SRAM (L2/L3/scratchpad arrays), NoC
ladder.gran: 1 mW; the PMIC's running average (τ ≈ 1 s) of each regulator's output power, copied by the SP every 133 ms; min and max since the last reset
ladder.note: Three PMBus regulators only: minion, SRAM, NoC, and their output side (w_out). DDR, VDDQ, PCIe, IO shire and Maxion have set-point registers and no current or power telemetry. The PMIC also holds v_in, a_in, w_in and a_out for the three, which the SP reads (84 values a pass) and does not forward. The 133 ms is the SP's loop, not the PMIC's, and a firmware artifact: the SP's I2C driver busy-waits 1 ms after every transaction. ettelem --reset-ms reads the min/max over a chosen window.

ladder.what: pJ per L1/L2/L3/DRAM load, per FMA slot
ladder.gran: ≥ 10⁹ identical events/s for 3 s bursts bracketed by idle; bars ±6% (median) over passes and cards
ladder.instrument: regression of rail power against counted events
ladder.note: The energy manual: 386 configurations, three shuffled passes on each of two cards, idle from the brackets, a leakage correction for the burst's own warming, bursts with the clock off 600 MHz discarded. One L1 load (≈50 pJ) is a million times below the floor and one DRAM line (≈8 nJ) ten thousand times; a single bit flip (~10⁻¹⁶ J) is 10¹² times below it.

ladder.what: DDR, L2/L3, PCIe DMA bandwidth and core utilisation
ladder.gran: 1 ms samples, chip-wide
ladder.note: The master minion's statistics worker (MMST trace) stops and restarts every shire-cache and memory-shire counter every 1 ms.

ladder.what: 35 temperature sensors, 125 voltage sense points (3 per minion shire, 2 per memory shire, IO and PCIe shires), 35 process detectors
ladder.gran: hardware 0.06 °C (12-bit) / 75 µV (14-bit); host sees 34-shire avg/low/high at 1 °C / 1 mV every 133 ms
ladder.note: Moortec PVT: 5 controllers, each 8 temperature sensors, 2 voltage monitors of 16 channels, 8 process detectors. Per-shire voltages leak out today as DEBUG log strings through DM_CMD_SET_DM_TRACE_CONFIG (the per-shire voltage map in Power and temperature, §3); per-shire temperature needs a firmware change; the process detectors are configured with measurement disabled and never read; two external analog VM inputs have a stub reader and no caller. No sensor measures current.

ladder.what: The 0.8 V memory-shire supply as the Moortec monitors in the 8 memory shires see it, 1 mV, every 133 ms
ladder.gran: 0.84 mV per watt of off-rail DRAM power, fitted over 386 configuration means (rms 0.36 mV): 1 mV ≈ 1.2 W
ladder.note: A voltage that droops with current is a current meter once its load line is known; this one is calibrated against the regression of §4, so it is not independent of the board meter, but it moves mostly with DRAM traffic (mesh traffic adds up to about 1.7 mV), every 133 ms. Other rails leak in at 0.025 mV per board watt.

ladder.what: The part of board power on no rail sensor, split into delivery losses of the metered rails and a per-byte DRAM cost
ladder.gran: rms 0.35 W over 392 configuration means (1.1 W on the 17 DRAM ones); coefficients ±1.4% (minion), ±2% (DRAM), ±7–33% (NoC, SRAM)
ladder.instrument: regression of (board − rails) against rail powers and DRAM bytes (§4)
ladder.note: Not a sensor: an attribution. It cannot say how the DRAM term splits between the DDR PHY, the I/O rail and the DRAM chips, nor how the idle 12–15 W splits between DDR, PCIe, the IO shire and the regulators' own draw.

ladder.what: v_in, a_in, w_in and a_out of the minion, SRAM and NoC regulators
ladder.gran: 1 mW class, per 133 ms record, already read by the SP
ladder.instrument: PMIC PMBus statistics (pmic_get_pmb_stats) forwarded by a new SP stats field
ladder.note: Would turn the fitted 18–20% delivery loss of §4 into a measurement per rail and per load, and shrink the unmetered remainder to the rails that truly have no meter.

ladder.what: Correctable/uncorrectable errors in shire-cache SRAM and I-cache; DRAM and PCIe counters
ladder.gran: per event; which 64-bit doubleword of a line, not which bit
ladder.note: Wired but dark: DRAM ECC is compiled off, and the SP never enables the PLIC sources for SRAM/I-cache errors, so those counts stay 0. L1D, tensor scratchpad and register files have no ECC or parity at all.

ladder.what: Retired instructions per thread, L1D misses, I-cache requests/misses
ladder.gran: per launch, summed over a neighbourhood of 8 minions
ladder.note: Events are fixed at boot; mhpmevent is M-mode. 32 minion and 25 neighbourhood events exist in the RTL, bit-exact with the PRM table.

ladder.what: Minion clock cycles, free-running
ladder.gran: 1 cycle (1.67 ns at 600 MHz)
ladder.note: Two counters per neighbourhood (even and odd harts), not synchronised across neighbourhoods. The late carry into bit 7 is a design property: 12 counters share one adder that folds pre-counter overflows in round-robin, and reads ignore the pending overflow bit. Reproduced from the open RTL in rtl-sim/pmu_carry. fixcyc() repairs host-corrected pairs; inside a kernel ~1.4% of timed intervals are still ±128 off, so reject those. Reading the standard cycle, time and instret CSRs from a kernel traps.

ladder.what: Load-to-use latency of one load after placing its line in L1/L2/L3/DRAM
ladder.gran: 1 cycle, one load
ladder.note: This is how the memory-anatomy report split a DRAM load into cache, mesh, controller and row-state parts to ±3 cycles for 97% of lines.

ladder.what: Software events with a cycle stamp: strings, values, PMC snapshots, profile regions
ladder.gran: 1-cycle stamp; ~20–40 cycles per entry (estimate)
ladder.note: A sink, not a new resolution. scripts/trace-flamegraph.py now turns profile events into per-hart flame graphs in cycles (workloads/traceprof: 512 events from 32 harts in 0.15 s of card time). Stamps come from the neighbourhood's even- or odd-hart hpmcounter3, each reset separately at boot, so they compare only between harts sharing a counter.

ladder.what: Per-bank reads/writes/cycles; per-memshire NoC reads/writes at 933 MHz
ladder.gran: one 40-bit counter per syscall (hundreds of cycles); chip-wide
ladder.note: Only the boot-time qualifiers. The memory-shire monitor can count DRAM activates, precharges and refreshes per bank, and the shire cache can measure queue occupancy (mean miss latency by Little's law), but selecting those needs M-mode.

ladder.what: L1 access/miss per thread, L2 miss rejections, tensor waits; L2/L3 hit/miss and occupancy; DRAM command counts
ladder.gran: same counters, any event
ladder.instrument: a new U-mode syscall writing mhpmevent / sc_perfmon / ddrc_perfmon
ladder.note: Written and verified in the simulator: patches/0003 adds a U-mode syscall (about 60 lines in four files), and workloads/pmcsel shows hpmcounter6 switching to a chosen event with the rebuilt firmware. Running it on the card needs a signed image.

ladder.what: GPRs, PC, seven CSRs, 8-byte memory words of a halted hart; hardware PC breakpoint
ladder.gran: 64 bits per management round trip (ms); halt unit = one neighbourhood (16 harts)
ladder.note: In every shipped BL2 variant and the node is 0666, but dev_mngt_service refuses the commands: a ~100-line libDM client is needed. Hazards: a halted worker wedges its kernel, RESET_HART is a stub, the debug clock is gated at boot. Rehearse on sys_emu first.

ladder.what: One instruction per resume of a halted hart
ladder.gran: 1 instruction per ms-scale round trip
ladder.note: The ENABLE_SINGLE_STEP command is a stub, but dcsr is writable by raw address. Erratum 1.18: safe only for harts 0/1 of a neighbourhood. Untested here.

ladder.what: Trap on any instruction matching a mask, log state, resume
ladder.gran: 1 instruction, hundreds of cycles of perturbation
ladder.note: A software single-step or a tensor-op logger without the debugger. PRM §14.1's 0x1C cause is a typo for 30.

ladder.what: Read or write one 128-bit quadword of L2/L3/scratchpad with its check bits
ladder.gran: one quadword per M-mode transaction
ladder.note: The closest thing to reading a stored bit on silicon, and a deliberate bit-flip injector (write with wrong ECC, read through the normal path).

ladder.what: Run one shire at a different clock to attribute the minion rail's power to it
ladder.gran: per shire, 25 MHz steps; ~0.3 W resolvable against a 1 mW LSB
ladder.instrument: per-shire LVDPLL and clock mux ESRs via SP firmware
ladder.note: The mux and PLL exist per shire, but the shipped firmware puts every shire on the chip-wide step clock, and erratum 7.3 calls the LVDPLL unstable on A0.

ladder.what: Instantaneous rather than averaged rail power, 10–50× faster loop
ladder.gran: tens to a few hundred Hz
ladder.instrument: SP firmware: drop the 84-read PMB snapshot, fix the 1 ms I2C busy-wait
ladder.note: The values are already read and discarded each pass. External: a scope on the LTC4218 IMON pin gives board total at ~kHz.

ladder.what: Every instruction with every register, lane, mask, memory and CSR write
ladder.gran: per instruction; no cycles, no cache contents
ladder.note: The same emulator is the golden model the RTL was verified against. The README's 'Fetched instruction' line is stale; the real line is I(prv): pc (bits) disasm.

ladder.what: Instruction trace per cycle, 128 selected signals per neighbourhood, 200 memory-controller signals
ladder.gran: per cycle, selected signals
ladder.instrument: UltraSoC status monitors and trace encoders over JTAG/USB
ladder.note: Real logic on the die; the IP, protocol and Data Book are not open, nothing configures it, and boot clock-gates it.

ladder.what: Full flop state of a shire via scan chains
ladder.gran: one dump, clock stopped, state destroyed
ladder.note: Designed in, with errata on the chain routers; no ATPG patterns or chain descriptions are open.

ladder.what: Every net, flop and SRAM bit of one neighbourhood (8 minions, VPUs, L1, I-cache) per clock
ladder.gran: 1 simulated cycle; toggle counts per signal
ladder.note: Verilator 5.042 now builds here without root, and single open-RTL modules simulate with waveforms (rtl-sim/pmu_carry runs neigh_pmu.v and explains a silicon bug; rtl-sim/fma_toggle counts the multiply-add flips behind the Horace experiment). The full 8-minion bench still needs its missing verilator.mk and cosim library; the main branch's whole-minion co-simulation references original files that are not in the public drop. No shire cache, NoC or DRAM; no cell library, so no joules.

ladder.level: Individual bit toggling on the fabricated chip
ladder.what: Watching one node switch in real time
ladder.note: The honest boundary. Everything above it is the answer.

contrast.et: Every instruction's 32-bit encoding is in the PRM; objdump names the custom CSRs; kernels are plain ELF.
contrast.gpu: PTX is documented; SASS is opcode names only. Encodings and control bits were reverse-engineered by third parties.
contrast.src: PRM §2.4; NVIDIA CUDA Binary Utilities; Jia et al. 2018

contrast.et: 13 design documents (541 pages) plus the RTL: pipeline stages, miss handlers, VPU latencies, PMU implementation.
contrast.gpu: Whitepapers and tuning guides; latencies and cache geometry come from microbenchmark papers.
contrast.src: core-et/docs; NVIDIA whitepapers; Luo et al. 2024

contrast.et: hpmcounter3 per neighbourhood, 1 cycle, with a documented (here) carry bug.
contrast.gpu: clock64() per SM, 1 cycle; %globaltimer counts in 32 ns steps but updates about once a microsecond (NVIDIA forum; the PTX manual gives no resolution).
contrast.src: this report; CUDA Programming Guide; NVIDIA developer forum

contrast.et: Fixed neighbourhood events in U-mode; per-bank cache and per-memshire counters by syscall; events selectable with a firmware change.
contrast.gpu: Nsight/CUPTI per-SM, per-L2-slice, per-FBPA aggregates; PC sampling; no per-bank/row or per-request data.

contrast.et: PA bits → L3 home shire, memory shire, bank, row, column, from the PRM and firmware, confirmed by counters.
contrast.gpu: L2 hash and DRAM bank/row mapping undocumented; recovered by timing (GPUHammer 2025).

contrast.et: Board power every 133 ms at 10 mW, plus three rails as the PMIC's ~1 s running average at 1 mW; no energy counter.
contrast.gpu: One board number: a 25 ms average every 100 ms on A100/H100; a mJ energy counter; no rails.
contrast.src: NVML docs; Yang et al. SC'24; this project's power-telemetry notes

contrast.et: L2/L3/I-cache SECDED with error logs (dark at this firmware); no L1D or register ECC; DRAM ECC off.
contrast.gpu: ECC on register file, L1, L2, HBM; counts per location, no syndrome or bit position.
contrast.src: PRM Tables 15-77 and 15-81; NVIDIA Memory Error Management r575

contrast.et: MDI: halt, breakpoint, GPR/CSR/memory of a hart, via the service processor; no gdb server for silicon (sys_emu has one).
contrast.gpu: cuda-gdb: breakpoints, warp single-step, register reads; no watchpoints.

contrast.et: Service processor and minion runtime are source; images are signed, key not open.
contrast.gpu: GSP firmware is a signed binary; user-mode driver closed.

contrast.et: Functional emulator with per-instruction state; RTL of the core with waveform dumps and lockstep cosim.
contrast.gpu: None. Accel-Sim is a tuned performance model driven by SASS traces.

reports.title: Limits of observability (this page)
reports.what: The hub: every instrument on the card, what it resolves, what it cannot see, the unmetered power attributed, and the ladder of improvements.

reports.title: Heat per millimetre
reports.what: The energy of moving one bit one millimetre across the mesh, with the data on the links chosen: per bit that differs from the previous flit, per one carried, and the part no data changes, on contended and uncontended links, against Dally's ~100 fJ/bit·mm.
reports.instruments: board power, NoC rail, die temperature, the sampler's latency; the die plot for millimetres per hop

reports.title: The energy manual
reports.what: Energy per instruction, per byte at every level, per message, per atomic, with confidence bars from repeated passes on two cards; the idle law; wires, lines, rows, leakage of the arrays, rails.
reports.instruments: board power, rails, die temperature, cycle counter; the leakage law

reports.title: The DVFS loop and its leakage
reports.what: The governor's states and thresholds, the three operating points, the idle law P<sub>idle</sub> = 12.6 W + 23.3 W·e<sup>(T−80)/36</sup> (aifoundry2), the rail split of idle, the activity term; aifoundry3's firmware reports a TDP of 0 W and that card never leaves 600 MHz; the open RTL's per-minion sleep controls are tied off and the card shows no array power gating.
reports.instruments: board power, rails, SP trace, DM_CMD config reads, driver ioctl

reports.title: The Horace experiment
reports.what: Same matmul, same FLOPs: 38 W on zeros, 47 on ones, 63 on random data; RTL flip counts predict the power to 0.5 W rms (leave-one-out); a flips-to-temperature model; from a cool die zeros run 25% faster; 14 structured matrices priced before they ran; the model carries to a second card with one scale factor.
reports.instruments: board power, die temperature, RTL simulation of the multiply-add unit

reports.title: Why is the ET-SoC-1 low power?
reports.what: Esperanto's P = C·V²·f + leakage measured term by term through ablations at 80 °C and set against an A100: voltage and clock give 5–6× less switching power, 1,024 cores in an integer loop add 1.5 W, leakage is 23 W of the 36 W idle, and per FLOP the card still spends more energy than the A100's bf16 tensor cores.
reports.instruments: board power, rails, preheated strict starts

reports.title: Power and temperature telemetry
reports.what: The first look at the meters: every way to read power, voltage and temperature and what each resolves; board power every 133 ms and three rails behind the PMIC's ~1 s average; idle power that rises with die temperature; the 34-shire voltage map from the SP's DEBUG trace.
reports.instruments: board power, rails, die temperature, SP stats and DEBUG traces

reports.title: Hand it to the next shire
reports.what: A multi-stage relay: handing each stage's output to the next shire runs 12× faster than a round trip through DRAM, at a twelfth of the energy per byte, and keeping it in the shire's own scratchpad about 31× faster; which shire receives the slab makes no difference to bandwidth (the next shire by ID is 1–10 mesh hops away, 3.5 on average; what each hop costs in energy is in Heat per millimetre).

reports.title: One hot line stops a shire
reports.what: One contended global atomic: every shire, the host included, gets its fair share (0.998–1.004) at one atomic per 10 cycles, while the host shire's own loads fall to 0.02% of normal; about 20 nJ per contended atomic, 17× a spread one.
reports.instruments: cycle counter, per-minion completion counts, board power

reports.title: Anatomy of a memory access
reports.what: One load taken apart to ±3 cycles for 97% of lines: the L3 home shire from PA[10:6], the memory shire from PA[8:6], DRAM banks, rows and refresh, and where the eight memory shires sit around the mesh; energy per load split by rail (since re-measured in the energy manual); the cycle counter's late-carry bug and its fix.
reports.instruments: evict_va + cycle counter, memory-shire read counters (syscall 10), board power, SP rail trace

reports.title: Memory hierarchy
reports.what: Latency, bandwidth and capacity of every level, next to the A100: L1 8.8 ns, L2 78 ns, L3 ~280 ns and DRAM ~490 ns at 600 MHz, 76 GB/s streaming. Its energy per byte now comes from the energy manual §4 (L2 2.51, L3 10.5, DRAM 122 pJ/B), which superseded the page's own 18 September figures.
reports.instruments: cycle counter, board power polled through dev_mngt_service

reports.title: On-chip communication
reports.what: Where the 32 shires sit on the 6×6 mesh (a round trip costs 150 cycles plus 12 per mesh hop, and a hop takes 20 ns at any clock); TensorSend/Recv, credits, barriers, reduction trees and rings: cycles per message, a 2.3 µs chip-wide allreduce, 7–34× less bandwidth between shires than inside one, and pJ per byte (re-measured in the energy manual §5).

reports.title: Matmul efficiency
reports.what: A tensor-unit matmul loop on cached tiles, all 1,024 minions: 9.5 TFLOP/s fp32, 19.0 fp16 and 71.8 TOP/s int8 (91–97% of peak), board power under load and a spec-sheet comparison with the A100; also the first hello world. Its operands are ±1 and ±2; the Horace experiment later showed that random data draws more power. (The scalar SGEMM is in Test drive.)

reports.title: Sparse compute
reports.what: What the tensor unit does with zeros: zero-skip saves power (86% in a TensorFMA loop on small integers) but never a cycle; masked loads and skipped empty slices take a batch-1 1024×4096 fp32 layer held in SRAM from 7.5 to 2.1 µs at 99% zeros; narrow lanes against divergence; six scenarios where the chip could beat an A100. Its power result is the one the Horace experiment later resolved into flips.
reports.instruments: cycle counter, board power polled through dev_mngt_service

reports.title: Ridge points
reports.what: Peak compute divided by each level's bandwidth: the operations per byte a kernel must do before compute, not memory, sets its speed. In fp32, 4 per byte from its own shire, 10 from L3 or another shire, 130 from DRAM (fp16 twice that, int8 eight times); what that takes for blocked matmul and for batch sizes; the limits that act like ridge points; energy balance points from the energy manual's measurements.
reports.instruments: none: arithmetic on the 18 Sep reports' data and the energy manual's

reports.title: Test drive
reports.what: First contact: the toolchain built on a Mac, hello worlds on the sys_emu simulator, a scalar fp32 SGEMM on aifoundry3's card (127 GFLOP/s on 2,048 harts, no SIMD or tensor unit), and three upstream issues found on the way.

reports.title: Spatial temperature: a brief
reports.what: The 35 Moortec temperature sensors on the 6×6 grid of minion, I/O and PCIe shires, the firmware's reduction to one whole-degree average, and the firmware changes a spatial heat map would need.
reports.instruments: none: firmware (353f20e) and RTL (b38a1a3) source reading

reports.title: L2 mainline starvation: a brief
reports.what: An argument written on 22 September, before the reproduction that afternoon, from a result that Ivan, another ET-SoC-1 programmer, reported in the AI Foundry Discord, and from the shire-cache spec: move hot shared lines to a shire that does not compute, and why a two-dimensional TensorSend systolic array hangs. Its 6% owner penalty was not reproduced: see One hot line stops a shire.
reports.instruments: none: the spec, the errata and a reported result

droop.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-catalogue-aifoundry2/telemetry.jsonl.gz (die_mv from DM_CMD_GET_ASIC_VOLTAGE: the Moortec voltage monitors averaged over the 8 memory shires for ddr, the 34 minion shires for minion/sram/noc)

host_sees.temperature: minion-shire average, low and high (integer °C); IO shire; PMIC
host_sees.voltage: minion-shire average of VDD_MNN, VDD_SRAM, VDD_NOC; memory-shire average of VDD_MS (as 'ddr'); IO shire VDD_MXN and VDD_0P75; PShire VDD_PSHR; the PMIC set points (integer mV)
host_sees.debug_trace: per-shire VDD_MNN/SRAM/NOC lines and per-memory-shire VDD_MS/NOC lines every loop pass at LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG
host_sees.not_exported: per-shire temperature, process detectors, external analog VM inputs

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Bracketed bursts with a leakage correction and a clock-excursion filter
improvements.adds: Idle from the stretches either side of each burst; the burst's own warming taken out with the idle law's slope; bursts in which the governor left 600 MHz discarded.
improvements.cost: done (energy manual, 23 Sep)
improvements.effect: Confidence bars of ±6% (median) on 386 entries; the first cool-card reruns, whose bursts spent 5–25% of their samples at 700–800 MHz, were caught by the filter and discarded.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Attribute the unmetered remainder by regression
improvements.adds: board − rails fitted over every configuration's mean as a loss per watt on each metered rail plus a cost per DRAM byte (§4).
improvements.cost: done (this page)
improvements.effect: Unmetered power above idle gets a name per configuration to 0.35 W rms (1.1–1.3 W rms on the DRAM configurations): 18–20% delivery loss on the minion rail, 68–73 pJ per DRAM byte off-rail. The idle 15 W stays unattributed.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Read the DDR rail's droop as a DRAM-power proxy
improvements.adds: die_mv.ddr (the memory shires' Moortec monitors) droops 0.84 mV per off-rail DRAM watt; the monitor is already in every ettelem sample.
improvements.cost: done (this page); calibration is the regression of rung 2
improvements.effect: DRAM activity every 133 ms at 1 mV ≈ 1.2 W, confounded by heavy mesh traffic; a second witness for the DRAM term.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Undo the rails' one-second average
improvements.adds: The PMIC's rail averages, as the SP forwards them, are roughly first-order (61% of a step at 1 s, 88% at 2 s). Inverting that filter sample by sample recovers rail power every 133 ms.
improvements.cost: ~50 lines in the analysis scripts; a calibration burst to pin τ
improvements.effect: Rail split of bursts shorter than 3 s; per-launch rail energy; the minion/SRAM/NoC split of transients.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Per-shire current maps from the DEBUG trace's IR drop
improvements.adds: The SP prints every minion shire's VDD_MNN/SRAM/NOC voltage each loop pass at LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG (the map in Power and temperature, §3). Calibrate each shire's drop against the rail meter with single-shire loads, and the map becomes current.
improvements.cost: a day: single-shire calibration bursts, a trace parser (sptrace exists)
improvements.effect: Where the metered watts go on the die, per shire, to about 10%; the spatial power map that the temperature sensors cannot give from the host.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Sub-degree temperature by step timing; min/max windows for peaks
improvements.adds: The integer die reading steps at sharp moments when polled at 10–45 Hz; fitting the heating that reproduces the steps gives rises that repeat to ±0.03 °C for a pattern heating the die by a degree or more (the Horace experiment); below half a degree it only bounds the rise. ettelem --reset-ms reads the PMIC's min/max over a window.
improvements.cost: done
improvements.effect: Thermal responses without a firmware change; peak power over any window.

improvements.group: software, on the data the card already gives
improvements.what: Watch the meter itself: its latency, and its queue
improvements.adds: Every ettelem sample records how long its six management commands took (took_ms). Bursts during which the service processor is starved — the s ↔ s+16 rings raise it from 22 ms to 150 ms and freeze the board reading; on aifoundry2, tensor loads between shires in the same column three hops apart raise it to about 1 s — are dropped. A sampler killed mid-request leaves its reply in the management queue and every later opener crashes on it: ettelem now exits cleanly on SIGTERM, and the runners drain the queue with one dev_mngt_service call and retry.
improvements.cost: done (23–24 Sep)
improvements.effect: One ring configuration and one column configuration on aifoundry2 were found to be unmeasurable this way; without the check the ring's energy read 45% low. The poisoned queue stopped the first start of the second heat-per-mm run on both cards; after the drain it ran 132 bursts per card with no sampler restart.

improvements.group: lab hardware, no firmware
improvements.what: A PCIe riser with shunts on 12 V and 3.3 V, read at a kilohertz
improvements.adds: An external meter of the card's input, 1 mW at 1 ms, that owes nothing to the PMIC's closed firmware and its 133 ms.
improvements.cost: a riser or interposer with sense resistors and an INA-class ADC, or a bench DAQ; a day; a slot in an open chassis
improvements.effect: The launch transients that widen the small-signal bars become visible and separable; 0.5 s bursts become measurable; the widest bars (the hot line's −15/+19%, the remote scratchpad's ±16%) narrow toward the 1–2% pass-to-pass scatter; the awake core and the DRAM relay are already at ±5–7%; the PMIC's own input-power reading gets an independent check.

improvements.group: lab hardware, no firmware
improvements.what: An infrared camera over the open card
improvements.adds: Which packages warm under which load: the DRAM chips, the DDR PHY side of the die, each regulator, the PCIe switch.
improvements.cost: a thermal camera and an open chassis; an afternoon
improvements.effect: The unmetered watts placed on the board: the split of the DRAM term between the PHY, the I/O rail and the chips, and of the idle 12–15 W between DDR, PCIe and the regulators, at least in proportion.

improvements.group: lab hardware, no firmware
improvements.what: A second card
improvements.adds: aifoundry3 repeats the catalogue, the reruns and the Horace protocol (not the DRAM-row runs).
improvements.cost: done
improvements.effect: The card factor: 0.95 over the catalogue (10–90%: 0.91–0.99); on the tensor unit's flip energies alone, 0.92 (the Horace experiment); bars that are mostly the card, not the day.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Forward the PMIC's input-side readings for the three metered rails
improvements.adds: v_in, a_in, w_in and a_out per regulator are already read by the SP every pass and dropped.
improvements.cost: a few lines in the SP stats structure, and a firmware image
improvements.effect: The delivery loss measured per rail and per load instead of fitted; the unmetered remainder shrinks to the rails that have no meter at all.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Export the 35 temperature sensors per shire
improvements.adds: The spatial brief's three options: a trace field, a DM command, or a DEBUG log line like the voltage one.
improvements.cost: a few lines; a firmware image
improvements.effect: Heat maps on the 6×6 mesh (0.06 °C only if the raw 12-bit codes are exported; the driver's own values are whole degrees); heat flow between shires; per-shire leakage from the idle law.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Enable the process detectors and the two external analog monitor inputs
improvements.adds: 35 ring-oscillator process detectors (one per minion shire and the IO shire) are configured with measurement disabled and never read; two external analog channels of the voltage monitors have a stub reader and no caller.
improvements.cost: driver already written; a firmware image; for the external inputs, finding what the board wires to them
improvements.effect: Per-shire silicon speed and a leakage proxy that separates the card factor into process and voltage; possibly two board-level sense points.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Faster, unaveraged power in the SP trace
improvements.adds: Drop the 84-read PMB snapshot and the 1 ms I2C busy-wait; record the PMIC's instantaneous power rather than its average.
improvements.cost: a firmware image; the PMIC's own refresh rate is the next unknown
improvements.effect: Board and rail power at whatever rate the PMIC itself updates (unknown), without the one-second average.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: Enable the SRAM ECC interrupt sources (and DRAM ECC)
improvements.adds: The counters are wired and read as zero because the SP never enables their sources; DRAM ECC is compiled off.
improvements.cost: a firmware image, and a decision on DRAM capacity
improvements.effect: Bit errors become observable at the doubleword; the only bit-level detectors the silicon has.

improvements.group: firmware (a signed build; see the firmware caveat)
improvements.what: A U-mode syscall to choose counter events
improvements.adds: mhpmevent, shire-cache and memory-shire perfmon selection from a kernel.
improvements.cost: written and verified in sys_emu (patches/0003); a signed firmware image
improvements.effect: Per-shire and per-neighbourhood event counts under a workload, instead of the fixed five.

improvements.group: tooling against existing interfaces
improvements.what: A libDM client for the Minion Debug Interface
improvements.adds: Register and memory snapshots of halted harts, hardware breakpoints, and mhpmevent writes before a launch. Rehearse on sys_emu, which models the debug module.
improvements.cost: ~100 lines of C++ against /opt/et/lib/libDM; the in-tree gtests are complete examples; a quiet card and a reset plan agreed with the lab admin
improvements.effect: Architectural state of a hart on silicon.

improvements.group: tooling against existing interfaces
improvements.what: Verilator flow for the whole core-et bench
improvements.adds: Every flop every cycle of eight minions. Two single-unit benches already run: rtl-sim/pmu_carry explained the counter's carry bug, and rtl-sim/fma_toggle counts the multiply-add flips behind the Horace experiment.
improvements.cost: days of build repair
improvements.effect: Below-silicon views of anything the card measures.

improvements.group: research
improvements.what: A cell library and netlist for the RTL
improvements.adds: Toggle counts from the RTL bench become joules only with a library the drop does not contain.
improvements.cost: not in the open tree
improvements.effect: Energy per flip from simulation rather than from fits to board power.

improvements.group: research
improvements.what: Current sensing below the regulators
improvements.adds: Nothing on the die or the board measures the current of the DDR, VDDQ, PCIe, IO or Maxion rails; splitting them means shunts on the board.
improvements.cost: board rework: not for a shared card
improvements.effect: The last 12–15 W of idle, and the DRAM term's split, stay inferred.
